title: What Are the Armenian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Person's publish method: update the existing page in place and change its slug; the old URL still needs a confirmed 301 to the new one. Check legacy slugs and other ranking pages.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page in full with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch; SEO pulls its ranked keywords and status and checks weddedwonderland.com for legacy slugs and other ranking pages. Keep its traditions if sourceable; never reuse wording; drop errors; correct brand terms. Publish method: the existing page is edited in place and its slug changed; the 301 from the old URL must be confirmed.

Culture, not politics: no commentary on Armenia's conflicts or borders. Armenian customs are kept in Armenia and the diaspora (including Australia); regional or church differences only where sourced. Leave out virginity or 'proof' customs (e.g. the 'red apple').

Likely customs (brief finalises): matchmaking and the formal asking (khosk-kap or similar, as sources spell it); the engagement; the godparents (kavor and kavorkin); the bride's dressing and the groom's party collecting her; the Armenian Apostolic church crowning (crowns, the shared cup, the knot or cross); lavash on the couple's shoulders and plates broken at the door (UNESCO lavash 2014 only as UNESCO's text says); the welcome at the groom's home; music with the duduk (UNESCO 2008) and the Kochari dance (UNESCO 2017) only where UNESCO's text links them to celebrations. Armenian terms transliterated as sources give them.

Destination angle: Smartraveller Armenia checked live, including any higher-level areas (border regions); suggest only areas outside them; no political framing. Plus Armenian-Australian weddings at home. Legal steps from official sources only (Smartraveller; the Australian embassy or consulate that covers Armenia; Armenia's civil status registration agency where readable): whether a church wedding alone is legal, CNI, apostille, translation, recognition in Australia; same-sex marriage only from an official source. 'Check with the registry and the embassy, including any fees' where unreadable; 'as at November 2026'.

Sources: UNESCO, the Armenian Apostolic Church (Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin) official pages, Armenia's culture or tourism ministry, museums, Britannica, academic sources. Unsourced becomes 'often told' or is left out; no [[VERIFY]] on 'often told' customs. One honest framing line per section, not repeated 'described as'.
Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (lavash, pomegranates) labelled illustrative pending approval.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; no extra sourcing rounds. Google Drive disconnected; Firecrawl out of credits.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.
Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
